title: The Seven Eyes and the Cherubim
english: It shall say. The days of the intelligible realm possess greatness and abundance near the sun of righteousness, and this is due to the difference between those being illuminated and the light itself. For when the Lord says concerning the righteous one who 'dwells in the help of the Most High' (Ps 90:14): 'I will fill him with length of days,' we do not say that a long life is promised to the righteous one who desires to 'depart so that he may be with Christ' (2 Cor 5:8), as he says: 'Woe, that my sojourn has been lengthened' (Ps 118:77).

Indeed, history also struggles against such a view, since those honoring parents are not becoming long-lived in every way, it having been said to each: 'Honor your father and your mother, so that it may go well with you and you may be long of years upon the earth which the Lord your God gives you' (Ex 20:12). For one finds those keeping this commandment becoming short-lived and outside of life in a short time.

Therefore, since the spoken word is shown not to have [the meaning] as many suppose, that which is said in the Psalms concerning length of days, and as elsewhere in the God-breathed Scripture is like: 'He sought life and you gave him length of days unto the age and unto the age of the age' (Ps 35:9), and that in Proverbs: 'The righteous shall make many years in wealth' (Prov 10:6).

But that the increasing illumination and length of days is the prophet of the divine laws, Moses, saying to the God-lover: 'This is your life and the length of your days: to love the Lord your God with all your soul and with all your heart' (Deut 6:5). For since love that is attentive to God is luminous, it prepares long and great days, so that those participating in it find themselves having many-dayed and long-lasting [existence].

Compared to these days, the introductory gleams are found to be small days, which he who is not undervaluing will easily be tempted by, following the bright progresses. In whichs the one born will rejoice in 'joy inexpressible and glorified' (1 Pet 1:8), existing in 'fruit of the Holy Spirit' (Gal 5:22).

And what follows him who rejoices thus, or to see the tinny stone in hand, that is, in practice, of Zerubbabel, from whom the one from Abraham and David and finally from Mary, Jesus, is genealogically descended, who works through all things to be luminous and discerning.

Regarding those approaching him. He said there are seven eyes, observing and looking upon all the earth, especially when those dwelling on the earth learned to do righteousness, walking without blemish and working righteousness. That these look upon things by the Lord is learned from the Psalmist saying: 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears to their prayer' (Psalm 34:15).

The whole has seven divine eyes, being inherently perceptive; in this way also the most holy Cherubim, at whom God attends, according to the vision of Ezekiel, are eyed all over, it having been said they are full of eyes, just as they have eyes on their sides and on their faces for the inspection of superabundant and great wonders. The Cherubim are interpreted as a multitude of knowledge; from which it appears that they see what they know and what they look upon and impose.

See then that: 'Who has made it into small days?' (Zechariah 4:11) does not indicate a sparingly seen thing, but someone called by some specifically, and by others an individual, similarly to the apostolic word having thus: 'Every house is built by someone' (Hebrews 3:4).

And I answered and said to him: 'What are these two olive trees which are by the right side of the lampstand and by the two olive branches?' (Zechariah 4:12). And I inquired a second time and said to him: 'What are the two olive branches which are in the hands of the two golden pipes that pour out and bring up the golden oil-streams?' (Zechariah 4:13). And he said to me: 'Do you not know what these are?' And I said: 'No, Lord.' And he said: 'These are the two sons of stability who stand beside the Lord of all the earth' (Zechariah 4:14).

When the angel speaking in the prophet asked: 'What do you see?' he answered and said inquiringly: 'What are these two olive trees which are on the right and by the olive branches of the lampstand?' An answer not being given to him, he inquires a second time about the two olive branches which are in the hands of the two pipes that pour out and bring up the golden oil-streams. To whom the angel said: 'Do you not know what these are?' 'No, Lord,' saying the prophet, the angel said: 'These are the two sons of stability who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.'
For one having the beginning of initiation, it is not possible at all to know what are those on the right and by the olive branches.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vision of the Flying Sickle
english: The oil of the lamp; therefore, he asks a second time concerning two branches of the olive trees. It has been made clear in the previous discourses that the divine study is called olive, because of their fruit increasing and nourishing the light. 1.337 Since it is not possible to perceive through all the trunks and the shoots of the plants in question the one 'knowing and prophesying in part' (1 Cor 13:9), he approaches a second inquiry concerning two branches of olives; for only through these is it possible to have a knowledge that imposes the truth 'through a mirror and an enigma' (1 Cor 13:12), so that, having been benefited from the partial, he might at last be able to know what the olives actually are. 1.338 And since one interpretation of what those who explained the text took as the two olives was the discourse concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit, see if the branches of these olives would grasp what is attainable to the one knowing in part. For while there is the olive of Christ, the becoming of the Word into flesh would be a branch; and of the Holy Spirit, his introductory contemplation, which is called his 'earnest money' (2 Cor 1:22). 1.339 Having asked a second time about these, the one receiving God heard from the angel who initiates into the mysteries: 'Do you not know what these are?' To which the one hearing replied: 'No, Lord.' 'These,' he says, 'are the two sons of fatness; they shall present to the Lord all the earth' (Ps 65:16). 1.340 For just as, by way of the discourse concerning the Father, which is the lamp above the lamp, as has been interpreted a little earlier, so the discourse concerning the Son and the Holy Spirit is being matched to the contemplation of the Father's fatness, being its sons, as it is possible for one still in the body to know. 1.341 According to another interpretation, the mystical understanding of the God-breathed Scriptures is the fatness of the house of God, according to that which is said in the thirty-fifth Psalm to the Lord God: 'They shall be intoxicated from the fatness of your house' (Ps 65:5); and it is clear that 'those who hope in the wings of God' (Ps 91:4) are sons of men, being two sons: the one having come by circumcision, and the other according to the Gospel of Christ. 1.342 Understand, if you are able, to take two sons of fatness having been presented to the Lord, those seen in glory with Jesus on the mountain, Moses and Elijah (Matt 17:2-3), making manifest the Law and the Prophets. Just as there is a certain quality of firmness, so too is the word of the prophet who has been opened. He read in a secret book that Enoch and Elijah are the two sons of firmness, as it is fitting because they resemble others. For Enoch was translated so as not to see death, and Elijah was taken up, being carried by a chariot of fire and a horse 'as into heaven' (2 Kings 2:11). Considering these things as being by power like our own, though brief, we set forth the following of the prophet, desiring also to understand them, if the one who enlightens the prophet through revelations should 'give a word by the opening of our mouths' (Zechariah 10:2).

And I turned and lifted up my eyes; and I saw, and behold, a flying sickle. And he said to me, 'What do you see?' And I said, 'I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits in length and ten cubits in width.' And he said to me, 'This is the curse going out over the face of the whole earth; because every thief from this shall be judged until death, and every one who swears falsely by this shall be judged until death. And I will execute it,' says the Lord of all (Zechariah 5:4), 'and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of the one swearing falsely by my name, and it shall destroy in the midst of his house, and it shall consume him and his wood and his stones.'

Turning from the passing vision, I lifted up my eyes of the mind. And I see a flying sickle, having a length of twenty cubits and a width of ten cubits. This is the sickle which, he says, shows the vision concerning it: this is the curse, that is to say, the punishment, being brought upon all the earth, to cut and consume the thief and the perjurer. And behold the greatness of the instruction occurring through revelation, making manifest from the visible things the things not visible, and from the sensible things the things understood.

For when the just Judge is examining the righteous and the impious upon the ballot, giving to each according to his practice and his works, the things brought against the unrighteous and impious men for punishment, where he names a sword and arrows, and elsewhere an axe and a sickle. When, therefore, 'the wicked and sorcerous men' and with them the predatory demons, being hostile and seditious because of the violence they possess, happen to be...

title: The Sickle of Judgment
english: Swords and spears are brought as appropriate punishment, as seen in the Great Song of Deuteronomy where the Lord says: 'I will drink my arrows from blood, and my sword shall be satiated with the blood of the wounded,' and also: 'I will strike them with my sword, and my arrows shall finish them.'

And since punishment touches not only those sinning upon the earth, but also angels who have fallen into wickedness—for it is written: 'God did not spare angels who sinned,' having left their heavenly home—it is said in Isaiah from the mouth of God: 'My sword was drunken in heaven.'

The impending judgment brought against the ungodly is most clearly known in Amos, the second of the Twelve Prophets, who says: 'All the sinners of the people shall perish by the sword.' For the prophetic word is not about a physical instrument of war, as it was never the case that all the sinners of the people were lifted up by a visible sword.

Equally, in the seventh Psalm, the singer threatens those called to repentance: 'If you do not turn away, he will make his sword shine; he has bent his bow, and prepared his weapons of death in it; he has made his arrows for those being burned.' Regarding the weapons of death, it is said in Jeremiah: 'How long will the sword of the Lord cut, how long will you not be at rest? Turn back to your slayer.'

Sufficiently having set forth the weapons of war that strike and harm the impious and rebellious men and even demons, let us see also what is announced enigmatically concerning trees not bearing good fruit, regarding the weapons of their wrath or their punishments. 'For make fruits worthy of repentance,' and also: 'Already the axe lies at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not making good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.'

According to these interpreted plants, the curse brings justice upon them in being cut down, those of whom it was said they bear destructive and harmful fruit: 'Our enemies are senseless. For their vine is the vine of Sodom, and their vine-branch is from Gomorrah; their cluster is a cluster of gall.'
[a] cluster of bitterness to them, their wine is the fury of dragons, and the unyielding fury of shields.

Regarding a choice of will, like a harmful vine producing poisonous fruits, it was necessary to cut it away with a sharp sickle, and to have the vine and the cluster removed. Since these things have been made more apparent, see also how each part is to be clarified as much as possible.

Turning back from what the prophet had already seen and taught, lifting up the luminous eyes of his heart, he sees a sickle flying, not perceptible to the senses, but understood clearly, having a length of twenty cubits and a width of ten cubits, cutting away 'every planting which the heavenly Father has not planted' (Matt 15:13). And everything being cut away turns out to be unclean.

The cutting is done with a sickle twenty cubits in length; for the number twenty is not pure, being two in tens. But since length does not remain alone, it takes on a width of ten cubits. And this number resembles a unity. It is shown through the measurements laid down that a blessed and profitable end occurs for those who are cleansed by means of the sickle.

The sickle is called a curse because it brings toil and injuries to those being cut down, bringing vengeance against everyone who steals and swears by the name of the Lord upon a lie. Therefore, if no one is to suffer these things, let him keep the commandments which are thus held, in the Mosaic teaching: 'You shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal' (Exod 20:14); and in the apostolic [teaching]: 'Let him who steals steal no longer, but rather let him toil, working for what is good' (Eph 4:28).

In the same way that theft must be avoided because of the curse called the sickle, so perjury must be fled from, 'not taking the name of the Lord in vain' (Deut 23:10). Shortly after the prophecy, perjury is forbidden thus: And those taking the name of the Lord upon a lie, 'and do not love a false oath' (Heb 12:2).

Concerning such a curse, the Lord says that the sickle exists: 'I will bring it to pass' by a vote of judgment, 'and it shall enter into the house of the thief and the perjurer, and it shall complete him, even his timber and his stones.' Just as the house being completed is not a sensible building, so too the things completing and making it whole—timber and stones—are not visible.
